prompt: Write prose.css for our documentation article body. The markup is `<article class="prose" lang="en">` containing h2, h3, p, ul and blockquote. The body face is Verdana (system font, no web font) and body text is 1.125rem on the browser's default root size; leave :root alone. Target about 66 characters per line, and keep a consistent vertical rhythm between headings and blocks. Save prose.css.
assertions: Rendered at a 1280px-wide viewport in Verdana with English sample prose, full body lines in .prose average between 58 and 74 characters

prose.css spaces blocks in a unit equal to one prose body line (1.125rem times the body line-height, e.g. a custom property or 1lh on the paragraph), not in rlh or rem values that resolve against the 16px root line
prose.css sets h2 and h3 margins as whole or half multiples of that same prose body line
prose.css sets the body font-size as a fixed rem value with no vw or vi term, so it doubles at 200% zoom
prose.css uses logical properties for every text-flow box property (no margin-left/right, padding-left/right, width or max-width on text, text-align: left/right)
prose.css sets h2 and h3 line-heights so each heading line is a whole or half multiple of the body line, so blocks after a wrapped heading land back on the body interval
prose.css gives an h3 that directly follows an h2 at least one body line of space above it
